governanceNotes: D1 batch 67 (2026-09-26): one bounded association edge authored - ovarian-cysts to menstrual-disorders (rank 1) - classified ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, and hypothesizedOnly:true. The proposition rests on the 169-patient abnormal-uterine-bleeding pelvic ultrasound cohort in which ovarian cysts were the most common reproductive-age sonographic finding (27.11% early, 22.56% late reproductive; majority likely benign; PMID 42257258).

Counter-evidence and caveat screens recorded 2026-09-26: (i) ascertainment direction - the cohort conditions on bleeding at presentation, so cyst-before-bleeding ordering is unestablished and the association is co-occurrence only; (ii) PCOS separation - polycystic ovarian morphology and PCOS are distinct (PCOS owns its own identity and its tumour-risk and anovulation literature is not recycled here); (iii) withheld cancer proposition - malignant-transformation evidence is case-level and the quantified endometrioma-cancer risk belongs to the endometriosis window (PMID 24518590), so no ovarian-cancer edge was authored; (iv) withheld pain proposition - pelvic-pain evidence is endometrioma-scoped with endometriosis as the shared substrate (ESCOMA sclerotherapy protocol), withheld on shared-substrate and ME-29 grounds; (v) withheld no-identity propositions - adnexal torsion, cyst rupture with hemoperitoneum, and infertility are documented ovarian-cyst complications without catalog identities (withheld propositions, not deferred identities).

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Ovarian cysts are documented among the leading structural findings in abnormal uterine bleeding at retrospective ultrasound-cohort level: the pelvic ultrasound study of 169 patients presenting with abnormal uterine bleeding at a tertiary hospital (2018-2020) found ovarian cysts the most common sonographic finding in both early and late reproductive groups (27.11 and 22.56 percent respectively), with the majority of cysts likely benign and fibroids dominant in the menopausal group (PMID 42257258); recorded as documented association only with the direction and ascertainment limits carried openly.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual: the anchor sampled women already presenting with bleeding (ascertainment conditioned on the outcome) so it cannot establish that cysts preceded the bleeding, functional cysts and anovulation are interdependent rather than sequential, and polycystic ovarian morphology is a distinct entity excluded from this mapping scope, so individual claims require dated pelvic imaging and endocrine evaluation with ovulatory, contraceptive, structural, and pregnancy exclusion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Functional follicular cyst persistence with anovulation drives unopposed estrogen exposure and irregular progesterone withdrawal so disordered endometrial shedding and irregular bleeding result, the anovulatory-hormonal route consistent with the cyst predominance among reproductive-age abnormal-bleeding ultrasounds, but whether this route produced any individual bleeding episode remains hypothesized until imaging and endocrine records are reviewed.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The association is supported at single retrospective ultrasound cohort class only: the cohort is conditioned on abnormal bleeding at presentation so no relative risk or predictive value is derivable, findings are sonographic without hormonal or histologic confirmation, and the cysts were likely benign functional entities in the majority with no temporal documentation of cyst-before-bleeding.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Ascertainment is conditioned on abnormal bleeding at presentation so direction cannot be established (cysts may be incidental findings); no hormone assays or ovulation documentation accompany the ultrasound findings; the majority of cysts were likely benign functional entities; PCOS and polycystic ovarian morphology are excluded scope but frequently overlap clinically; and uterine fibroids, endometrial pathology, contraceptive effects, pregnancy, coagulopathy, and thyroid disease compete for individual attribution.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: polycystic ovary syndrome and polycystic ovarian morphology (distinct catalog identity; expressly excluded scope)
uterine fibroids and endometrial pathology (dominant findings in the menopausal group)
contraceptive and medication effects on bleeding patterns
coagulopathy, thyroid disease, and perimenopausal anovulation

suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at retrospective ultrasound-cohort class with the direction and ascertainment limits carried openly: the 169-patient abnormal-uterine-bleeding ultrasound cohort found ovarian cysts the most common reproductive-age finding (27.11 and 22.56 percent; PMID 42257258); because the cohort is conditioned on bleeding at presentation, lacks hormonal confirmation, and cannot order cyst-before-bleeding, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only, excludes polycystic morphology from scope, and routes individual claims through dated pelvic imaging and endocrine evaluation with ovulatory, contraceptive, structural, and pregnancy exclusion.
